ops.task_class: checklist-engine mechanics (any role driving a gated/survey checklist)
ops.statement: A `command`-kind postcondition (`check: {"kind": "command", ...}`) is REFUSED by `attest` ("engine-checked; cannot attest"). The engine runs the command check itself DURING `advance` on that task — the caller should run the check independently for their own confidence, then call `advance` directly with `--why`; there is no separate attest step for a command-kind condition. Only `null`-check and `artifact`-kind conditions are satisfied by `attest`/`attach` ahead of `advance`.
ops.grounding: Reproduced 3x independently in run 117-curate: g1-implementer's IMPLEMENTER_RESULT Workflow Feedback (.agent-work/117-curate/g1-implement-result.md) names this exact refusal and workaround; the Commander (this run) hit the identical refusal attempting `attest g1-integrate --cond c1` and `attest g2-integrate --cond c1` (both command-kind test-suite checks) and resolved it the same way, satisfying c1 purely via the subsequent `advance` call.
ops.bank_reason: Understood and reproducible, but the fix is a doctrine-wording change (the spine/plan template's gN-integrate imperative, or checklist-engine.md's own phrasing) — applying a docs/agents-style doctrine delta requires human authority per this skill's own rule, unavailable in this delegated run (no reachable human this session). Banking until a human curator/Charter-refresh pass can apply the wording fix; re-observation across a few more runs would also confirm whether this trips every command-kind gate uniformly or only specific ones.
